rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the primary uncertainty is whether a standard multimodal multiprofile pipeline can establish a strong performance baseline. Config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA n2000, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) uses well-established, robust components across all design axes, minimizing the risk of a poor result due to a single weak choice. It tests the core hypothesis that combining RNA and image modalities with multiprofile aggregation yields competitive accuracy. Establishing this baseline is critical: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can systematically upgrade individual components (e.g., swap to ViT-L, transformer aggregation, scvi/scgpt encoders) to identify what drives gains; if it underperforms, it flags that the basic multimodal architecture needs rethinking. As experiment 1 of 10, this maximizes information per trial by anchoring the search around a reliable reference point.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieved 63.9% accuracy, giving us a baseline but no information about which image encoder is superior. Uncertainty: The image encoder is a critical design choice—ResNet50 (~25M params) vs. ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L (~300M params) represent a large capacity gap, and we don't know whether the stronger image features translate to better multimodal fusion performance. This experiment (config_006) changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while holding all other settings identical to config_001, making it a clean single-variable ablation. Rationale: With 8 experiments remaining, establishing whether the image encoder is a major lever early will guide the bulk of subsequent experiments. If ViT-L substantially improves accuracy, we can focus the remaining budget on optimizing around it (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion); if not, we save experiments by not exploring that branch. This is the highest-information single experiment available given the sparse evidence.

Evidence: Both completed experiments (config_001, config_006) used pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder with multimodal/multiprofile/avgpool/weighted settings, yielding ~0.635-0.639 accuracy. The only tested variable was image encoder (resnet50 slightly ahead of ViT-L by 0.4%). The RNA encoder choice remains completely unexplored, and it is a fundamental representation decision that could substantially shift performance. Question: config_025 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding all other settings identical to config_001 (resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile), providing a clean single-variable ablation. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether a learned generative RNA representation (scvi) outperforms a linear one (PCA) is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact question. A positive result would justify further exploration of scvi-based configs; a null or negative result would confirm PCA sufficiency and redirect budget toward aggregation/fusion or profile-setting variations.

Evidence: config_025 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the clear best at 0.6776, showing scvi_n200 is a strong RNA encoder (~4% over pca_n2000). The image encoder choice (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) showed only a small difference in the pca_n2000 setting, so resnet50 remains a reasonable default. Uncertainty: whether the aggregation strategy (avgpool vs transformer) matters when paired with the stronger scvi_n200 encoder. This experiment (config_014: scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) tests transformer aggregation as a single-variable change from the current best, keeping all other proven components fixed. A transformer aggregator can model inter-profile interactions in the multiprofile setting, potentially capturing complementary information that simple averaging discards. With 6 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value exploitation step: it directly extends the best configuration along the most impactful untested architectural axis, and a positive result would establish a new best to build upon.

The best result so far is config_014 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted; acc=0.713). The evidence strongly supports transformer aggregation (+0.035 over avgpool) and scvi_n200 (+0.039 over pca_n2000). The key remaining uncertainty in this top-performing regime is the image encoder: with pca_n2000+avgpool, resnet50 and imagenet_vit_l were nearly tied, but under transformer aggregation the larger ViT-L's richer representations may interact differently. Config_024 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a single-variable change from config_014, directly testing whether imagenet_vit_l can push accuracy beyond 0.713. This is the highest-value exploitation step: it extends the strongest configuration along the one untested axis, and with 5 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the image encoder choice early allows the remaining budget to focus on further refinements (e.g., fusion strategy or scgpt) if needed.

The current best (config_024: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.725) clearly establishes that scvi_n200 > pca_n2000, transformer > avgpool, and imagenet_vit_l ≥ resnet50. The only untested variation within this top-performing family is the fusion method (concat vs. weighted). Config_002 isolates exactly this question: does concat fusion outperform weighted fusion given the same encoders and transformer aggregation? This is the lowest-risk, highest-information experiment: if concat improves accuracy, we immediately beat 0.725; if not, we confirm weighted is optimal and can pivot remaining budget toward exploring scgpt as an alternative RNA encoder. With only 4 experiments left, exploiting the strongest known direction while resolving the last untested knob is the most efficient use of the next slot.

The evidence strongly shows that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_024, acc=0.725) is the current best, and that transformer aggregation, imagenet_vit_l, and weighted fusion are the preferred settings. The largest remaining uncertainty is whether the scgpt RNA encoder can outperform scvi_n200, since scgpt has not been tested in any completed experiment. Config_041 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) isolates this single variable while holding all other dimensions at their empirically best values. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new high-accuracy direction for the remaining 3 experiments; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 as optimal and lets us redirect remaining budget to fine-tuning other aspects (e.g., fusion or profile setting). This is the highest-information experiment available under the limited budget.

Evidence: The top-performing family is scvi_n200 + transformer aggregation, with config_024 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) at 0.7250 as the current best. We know weighted slightly edges concat for imagenet_vit_l (0.7250 vs 0.7207), and resnet50 trails imagenet_vit_l under transformer+weighted (0.7131 vs 0.7250). Question: config_032 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat) is the last untested combination within the proven scvi_n200 + transformer family, testing whether concat fusion interacts differently with resnet50's feature space. Why this is the best use: With 2 experiments remaining after this one, I need to either confirm the optimal configuration or find a surprise. This is the highest-expected-value untested config in the dominant family—it directly tests the one remaining fusion/encoder interaction that could plausibly rival or exceed 0.7250, while also tightening our understanding of whether weighted is strictly superior to concat across image encoders, informing the final two experiments.

The current best (config_024: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) has been well-established, and all scvi_n200+transformer variants have been exhausted. The strongest remaining untested combination is config_045 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted), which pairs the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion with the second-best RNA encoder. This tests whether the large transformer-aggregation gain observed with scvi_n200 (0.678→0.713/0.725) is generalizable or specific to scvi's learned representations. Given only 1 experiment remains after this, confirming the encoder-aggregation interaction is the highest-value information: if pca_n2000+transformer approaches scvi_n200 levels, it reveals the aggregation is the dominant factor; if it stays near 0.64-0.68, it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and solidifies config_024 as the final answer.

The current best is config_024 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250. All top-performing experiments share scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as encoders, with transformer aggregation providing a clear advantage over avgpool. The only untested variant that retains the two best encoders and the best fusion (weighted) is config_020, which switches to singleprofile (bypassing the aggregation step entirely). This tests whether the simpler singleprofile architecture—where the profile is handled without an explicit pooling/aggregation layer—could match or exceed the multiprofile + transformer pipeline. As the final experiment, this is the highest-value test: it either discovers a new best or definitively confirms that the multiprofile + transformer architecture is essential to the top performance, closing the search with full confidence in config_024 as the winner.
